title: linkaxes
summary: Link axes limits across multiple axes.

gpu_support.notes: `linkaxes` updates host-side graphics state only and does not execute numeric GPU kernels.

description: `linkaxes(ax)` links the x- and y-axis limits for a vector of axes handles. `linkaxes(ax, option)` links only the requested axis limits or removes existing links.
behaviors: `linkaxes(ax, 'x')` links X limits while leaving Y limits independent.
`linkaxes(ax, 'y')` links Y limits while leaving X limits independent.
`linkaxes(ax, 'xy')` links both X and Y limits.
`linkaxes(ax, 'off')` removes the supplied axes from any existing linked-axes groups.
When a new link is created, linked axes are synchronized to limits that encompass the current limits of every supplied axes handle for the linked axes.
Axis-specific links can overlap. For example, one axes can stay linked to another axes on X limits while also being linked to a different axes on Y limits.

examples.description: Link x limits for two subplots

faqs.question: Does `linkaxes` create axes?
faqs.answer: No. It requires existing axes handles such as values returned from `subplot`, `axes`, or `gca`.

faqs.question: Does linking affect future `set(ax, 'XLim', ...)` calls?
faqs.answer: Yes. Linked limits propagate through RunMat's central axes-limit state path, including `xlim`, `ylim`, `set`, and zoom-related limit updates. Unlinked axes continue to use the direct limit-update path.

gpu_residency: `linkaxes` works with host-side graphics handles and does not move arrays between host and GPU memory.
gpu_behavior: `linkaxes` performs no provider dispatch and has no GPU kernel implementation.
